title: S3 object locations rewrite object keys as folder prefixes

evidence.quote: S3Location(profileName: profileName, regionOverride: regionOverride, bucket: bucket, prefix: Self.normalizedPrefix(key, isFolder: false))

reasoning: S3 object keys are modeled through objectLocation(key:), but that method first applies path-like normalization and then passes the result into the public S3Location initializer. The initializer unconditionally normalizes as a folder, so an object key such as logs/app.txt becomes logs/app.txt/. The same normalization also strips leading slashes, collapses repeated slashes, trims whitespace, and maps dot-only keys to empty. BrowserItem exposes the resulting S3Item.location as the item's StorageLocation, so callers that navigate, persist, breadcrumb, or otherwise act on storageLocation can address a different S3 key or treat an object as a prefix.
recommendation: Separate folder-prefix normalization from object-key preservation. Add an initializer or factory that can store an already-normalized object key without appending a slash, and have objectLocation(key:) preserve exact object keys while prefix navigation continues to normalize folder prefixes.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included NavigationHistoryTests exercise only local URL history and do not assert S3Location.objectLocation or BrowserItem.storageLocation behavior for S3 objects.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a storage model test asserting that S3Location(profileName: "ops", regionOverride: "us-east-1", bucket: "bucket", prefix: "").objectLocation(key: "logs/app.txt").prefix == "logs/app.txt", and that BrowserItem.s3(object).storageLocation preserves the same object key without a trailing slash.
minimumFixScope: Grove/Models/StorageLocation.swift, with any S3 object construction call sites adjusted only as needed to preserve the object-vs-prefix distinction.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths still exist. The public S3Location initializer still normalizes folder prefixes at Grove/Models/StorageLocation.swift:47-51, and BrowserItem.storageLocation still returns the S3 item location at Grove/Models/BrowserItem.swift:119-124, but the defective objectLocation path changed: Grove/Models/StorageLocation.swift:109-115 now uses a private normalizedPrefix initializer instead of routing back through the public folder-normalizing initializer, so logs/app.txt is not rewritten to logs/app.txt/. Production S3 object items are built through location.objectLocation(key:) at Grove/Services/S3BrowserService.swift:768-778. A current regression test at GroveTests/StorageModelTests.swift:36-53 asserts objectLocation.prefix == "logs/app.txt" and BrowserItem.s3(item).storageLocation preserves that object location. I attempted the narrow Xcode test, but execution was blocked by the read-only sandbox before package resolution/result-bundle creation with Operation not permitted; the current source and regression test still support classifying this clawpatch finding as fixed.
